answer: Mechanism: peer-prediction scoring. A juror's reward depends not on an official key but on how well its grade predicts other independent jurors, scored by a proper rule so honesty maximizes payoff. Fake identities must genuinely understand each artifact to earn; bluffing buys statistical noise, the flat grey between facets of a prism where no color gathers. The attacker's best move is to grade honestly anyway, at which point its fleet is just unpaid labor. Quality seeks its zenith without any oracle, a terrace of aligned incentives where each stone holds the next in place.
